topic.name: Computing the Singular Values of a Matrix

question.text: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 \end{bmatrix}?$
question.explanation:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix $A^T \! A.$

First, we calculate $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} A^T \! A &= \begin{bmatrix} 3&-2 \end{bmatrix}^T \begin{bmatrix} 3&-2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 3\\-2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 3& -2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 9 & -6 \\ -6 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} |A^T \! A - \lambda I| &= 0 \\[5pt] \begin{vmatrix} 9- \lambda & -6 \\ -6 & 4- \lambda \end{vmatrix} & =0 \\[5pt] (9- \lambda)(4- \lambda) - 36 &= 0 \\[5pt] \lambda^2 - 9 \lambda - 4\lambda + 36 - 36&= 0 \\[5pt] \lambda^2 - 13 \lambda &= 0 \\[5pt] \lambda (\lambda - 13 ) &= 0 \\[5pt] \lambda &= 13, \, 0 \end{align*}

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

\begin{align*} \sigma_1 &= \sqrt{\lambda_1} = \sqrt{13} \\[3pt] \sigma_2 &= \sqrt{\lambda_2} = 0 \end{align*}

question.text: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1& -1\\ 0&1& -1 \end{bmatrix}?$
question.explanation:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix $A^T \! A.$

First, we calculate $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} A^T \! A &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1& -1\\ 0&1& -1 \end{bmatrix}^T \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1& -1\\ 0&1& -1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1& -1\\ 0&1& -1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} |A^T \! A - \lambda I| &= 0 \\[5pt] \begin{vmatrix} 1-\lambda & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2-\lambda & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 2- \lambda \end{vmatrix} & =0 \\[5pt] (1- \lambda) \begin{vmatrix} 2- \lambda & -2 \\ -2 & 2- \lambda \end{vmatrix} & =0 \\[5pt] (1- \lambda) \big( (2- \lambda)(2- \lambda) - 4 \big) &= 0 \\[5pt] (1-\lambda) (\lambda^2 - 4\lambda) &= 0 \\[5pt] -\lambda(\lambda - 1) (\lambda - 4) &= 0 \\[5pt] \lambda &= 4, \, 1, \: 0 \end{align*}

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

\begin{align*} \sigma_1 &= \sqrt{\lambda_1} = \sqrt{4} = 2 \\[3pt] \sigma_2 &= \sqrt{\lambda_2} = \sqrt{1} = 1 \\[3pt] \sigma_3 &= \sqrt{\lambda_3} = \sqrt{0} = 0 \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Singular Values of a Square Matrix

question.text: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix} 0&-1&2\\2&2&0 \end{bmatrix}?$
question.explanation:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix $A^T \! A.$

First, we calculate $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} A^T \! A &= \begin{bmatrix} 0&-1&2\\2&2&0 \end{bmatrix}^T \begin{bmatrix} 0&-1&2\\2&2&0 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 0&-1&2\\2&2&0 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 4 & 0 \\ 4 & 5 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} |A^T \! A - \lambda I| &= 0 \\[5pt] \begin{vmatrix} 4 - \lambda& 4 & 0 \\ 4 & 5 - \lambda& -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 4 - \lambda \end{vmatrix} & =0 \\[5pt] (4 - \lambda)\begin{vmatrix} 5 - \lambda & -2 \\ -2 & 4 - \lambda \end{vmatrix} - 4\begin{vmatrix} 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 4-\lambda \end{vmatrix} & =0 \\[5pt] (4 - \lambda)\left[(5 - \lambda)(4 - \lambda) - 4) \right] - 16(4-\lambda)&= 0 \\[5pt] (4 - \lambda)(\lambda^2 - 9\lambda + 16) - 16(4-\lambda)&= 0 \\[5pt] (4 - \lambda)\left( \lambda^2 -9\lambda\right) &= 0 \\[5pt] \lambda (4 - \lambda)(\lambda - 9) &= 0 \\[5pt] \lambda &= 9, \, 4, \: 0 \end{align*}

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

\begin{align*} \sigma_1 &= \sqrt{\lambda_1} = \sqrt{9} = 3 \\[3pt] \sigma_2 &= \sqrt{\lambda_2} = \sqrt{4} = 2 \\[3pt] \sigma_3 &= \sqrt{\lambda_3} = \sqrt{0} = 0 \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Singular Values of a Rectangular Matrix

question.text: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix} 1&1&0\\0&0&1 \end{bmatrix}?$
question.explanation:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix $A^T \! A.$

First, we calculate $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} A^T \! A &= \begin{bmatrix}1&1&0\\0&0&1 \end{bmatrix}^T \begin{bmatrix} 1&1&0\\0&0&1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1&1&0\\0&0&1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} |A^T \! A - \lambda I| &= 0 \\[5pt] \begin{vmatrix} 1-\lambda & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1-\lambda & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 - \lambda \end{vmatrix} & =0 \\[5pt] (1-\lambda)\begin{vmatrix} 1-\lambda & 1 \\ 1 & 1-\lambda \end{vmatrix} & =0 \\[5pt] (1 - \lambda)((1-\lambda)^2 - 1)&= 0 \\[5pt] (1 - \lambda)(1-2\lambda +\lambda^2- 1)&= 0 \\[5pt] - \lambda ( \lambda-1)(\lambda - 2) &= 0 \\[5pt] \lambda &= 2, \, 1, \: 0 \end{align*}

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

\begin{align*} \sigma_1 &= \sqrt{\lambda_1} = \sqrt{2} \\[3pt] \sigma_2 &= \sqrt{\lambda_2} = \sqrt{1} = 1 \\[3pt] \sigma_3 &= \sqrt{\lambda_3} = \sqrt{0} = 0 \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Singular Values of a Rectangular Matrix

question.text: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3 \end{bmatrix}?$
question.explanation:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix $A^T \! A.$

First, we calculate $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} A^T \! A &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3 \end{bmatrix}^T \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 \\ 2 & -3 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ -2 & -3 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 13 & 12 \\ 12 & 13 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} |A^T \! A - \lambda I| &= 0 \\[5pt] \begin{vmatrix} 13- \lambda & 12 \\ 12 & 13 - \lambda \end{vmatrix} & =0 \\[5pt] (13- \lambda)(13- \lambda) - 144 &= 0 \\[5pt] 169 - 26\lambda + \lambda^2 - 144 &= 0 \\[5pt] \lambda^2 - 26 \lambda +25 &= 0 \\[5pt] (\lambda-1) (\lambda - 25 ) &= 0 \\[5pt] \lambda &= 25, \, 1 \end{align*}

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

\begin{align*} \sigma_1 &= \sqrt{\lambda_1} = \sqrt{25} = 5 \\[3pt] \sigma_2 &= \sqrt{\lambda_2} = \sqrt{1} = 1 \end{align*}
